@graph.name: Frequently asked questions about laser tattoo removal

mainEntity.name: How does laser tattoo removal work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Laser tattoo removal uses concentrated light energy to break down tattoo ink particles in the skin. Over time, the body’s immune system flushes these particles out.
The sensation varies and is often compared to a rubber band snapping against the skin. Numbing creams or cooling devices are used to minimise discomfort.

mainEntity.name: How many sessions are needed for complete tattoo removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the tattoo’s size, ink colours and age, and on your skin type. On average, 6–12 sessions may be required.

mainEntity.name: Can all tattoo colours be removed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Darker colours such as black and blue are easier to remove, while lighter colours such as yellow, green and white can be more challenging.

mainEntity.name: Are there any side effects of laser tattoo removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common side effects include redness, swelling and mild blistering, which usually subside within a few days. Scarring is rare when the treatment is performed by a qualified professional.

mainEntity.name: Can laser tattoo removal be used on all skin types?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Modern lasers can treat a range of skin tones, but darker skin may need specialised settings to avoid pigmentation changes.

mainEntity.name: How long does each session take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A session typically lasts 10 to 30 minutes, depending on the size and complexity of the tattoo.

mainEntity.name: Can I resume normal activities after the treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but avoid direct sun exposure and strenuous exercise for a day or two after the treatment.
